event.title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
event.canonical_title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
event.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed openness to a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. This statement comes as King Charles continues his tour of the Caribbean, where discussions about the UK's colonial history are prominent. However, Burnham has ruled out the possibility of financial reparations, despite ongoing demands from Caribbean nations.

timeline.title: King Charles III Addresses Legacy of Slave Trade at Commonwealth Summit
timeline.summary: At a Commonwealth summit, King Charles III expressed his horror at the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade, describing it as a 'monstrous injustice' and a 'shameful chapter of history.' While he acknowledged a greater understanding of the horrors of slavery, he did not address calls for formal apologies or reparations. Prime Minister Andy Burnham indicated openness to the idea of the UK apologizing for its role in the slave trade.
